# Fixed finite retention corroboration

This separate route captures only the frozen selectors in SELECTORS.json. The packet and its new parsers are source under review; no capture, loader closure, SDK/tool execution, namespace confinement, native proof or managed-root diagnosis is qualified by this source checkpoint. The nine historical missing tracing edges and four pending source contracts remain unresolved. A changed runner file is a new input, even when its public spelling matches the historical inventory.

The workflow focus is `retention-corroboration`, with `b3_compile_only=true`, `b3_full_gate=false`, and binaries/resolver/additional-axiom flags false. Invalid flags produce routing diagnostics and do not invoke the packet. All thirteen existing jobs are excluded from this focus. The dedicated job checks captured route bytes before compiling that Python source; the route checks source and routing manifests before compiling exactly captured packet bytes. No inspected Python file, PE image, ELF image, configuration, SDK task, old inventory scanner, collector, analyzer, target or proof body is imported or executed. The packet contains no subprocess, network, dynamic-loader, namespace or archive-download call. Checkout and artifact delivery are workflow infrastructure; they are outside this in-process packet claim.

Ordinary isolated Python 3.12 startup and the explicitly declared stdlib imports do execute. XML/JSON/PE/ELF interpretation is newly authored Python code. The receipt states that interpreter source-to-binary closure is unqualified, lists declared loaded interpreter module paths, and does not claim that this packet rehashed every interpreter module. `-I -S -B` and captured-source execution exclude site/user imports and cached source substitution; they do not establish a complete interpreter/native dependency closure.

## Public source IDs

`P001` through `P086` are **one-based ordinals of the ordered `files` array in PRIMARY-SOURCE-PINS.json**. For example, P001 is its first entry, `dotnet/diagnostics` at commit `240cb1ce5bc30594c515206764241d7982e384af`, path `eng/Version.Details.xml`; P086 is its last entry. The exact manifest SHA-256 is `36526c27611aeeb2768bf946045f2c4d812fd153b0a9766fa74401f6756609c6`, also frozen as SELECTORS.json's `sourceIndexManifestSha256`. The packet checks that digest, the 86-entry denominator and the selector owner ordinals. Repo, commit, public path, byte count, SHA-256, Git blob and primary URL are detached in that manifest. A separate private review-location aid is not an executable input and is not needed to interpret these public IDs. These source pins are research provenance, not installed-binary source correspondence.

## Input bounds and accounting

The 265 filesystem selectors retain 263 unique spellings; the two duplicate spellings have separately reviewed roles. There are 101 historical Python module associations at 98 paths, 32 selected package names, six fixed shallow directory observations and five historical archive text roles. No config reference, metadata AssemblyRef, DT_NEEDED name or package file declaration adds a selector. Aliases can terminate only at a declared endpoint; unknown endpoints are not opened. Before content is opened or a directory is enumerated, every canonical ancestor is opened relative to its retained predecessor descriptor with O_DIRECTORY and O_NOFOLLOW, with stat/fstat identity checks. The final file opens relative to that retained parent with O_NOFOLLOW and is identity-checked before its first byte. The same descriptor rule covers source integrity, route integrity, workflow entry and fresh output directories. Post-read alias and file rechecks remain required. A symlink target with a parent step after another target component is explicitly unsupported: lexical normalization cannot establish traversal through an intervening alias. Leading parent steps from the already resolved source directory remain bounded. Absence is confirmed relative to an opened no-follow readable parent directory descriptor, bracketed by equal descriptor identities before and after that lookup. The earlier path lookup is only a hint; it is not the bracketed observation. Initial file/alias and absence observations have bounded final rechecks; those checks are observations within a changing filesystem, not permanent immutability.

The **128 selected text roles** consist of 28 SDK, 3 reference-pack, 11 Python, 17 public OS/config, 5 historical archive and at most 64 selected package-info roles. Each of those reads is at most 4 MiB. This includes parser input even if publication is withheld. Separately, `/var/lib/dpkg/status` is a single raw stream of at most **16 MiB** and at most 512 selected paragraphs; it consumes **zero** of the 128 role slots. Its captured bytes are charged **before UTF-8 decoding or paragraph parsing** to the **same 64 MiB aggregate text budget**. `inputTextReads` counts complete captured role reads; `statusTextBytes` counts complete status bytes; `inputTextBytes` counts both. Independently enforced `attemptedInputTextReads`, `attemptedInputTextBytes` and `attemptedStatusBytes` charge admitted role reads and every streamed block before digesting, parsing or retaining it. Failed, changed or partial reads never refund attempted bytes. Hash-file and source-control aggregate bytes are likewise charged per block, including failed captures. A complete accepted capture must reconcile attempted and complete text accounting. No aggregate exception is granted to status. Own source/control integrity reads are separately capped at 512 reads and 64 MiB; they do not grant further runner text roles. The five historical member source reads count toward both their selected text roles and source/control integrity accounting.

Hash input has a 512 MiB/file and 8 GiB aggregate bound, including final selected-file rechecks. New PE metadata is bounded to 16 MiB, with 256 AssemblyRef rows. Only compressed #~ metadata with no pointer tables is supported; #- and present pointer tables fail closed and are recorded as unsupported. At most three unique eligible custom attributes are admitted before copying or decoding their bounded known string-constructor values; no attribute is instantiated. Blob access uses bounded memory views rather than copying the whole heap for each row. ELF is limited to the exact eligible images, 8,192 dynamic entries, 256 needed names, no export enumeration and no dependency expansion. ET_REL remains catalogued outside the load graph. Exact shallow directories have the frozen immediate-entry caps and no unknown-entry descent. One 600-second work deadline is inherited from the workflow entry through the router and packet, followed by an independent 30-second packet finalization and one shared five-second packet/router publication window. Schema traversal, source reads, incremental parsers, output preflight and emission check their applicable deadline. The router has its own fixed 512-read/64 MiB control-integrity budget, outside the packet's separately bounded control phases; neither budget permits extra runner text roles. Workflow pre-invocation diagnostics contain only fixed small fields, are at most 2 KiB, and are not appended after route invocation. The first work fault is retained separately from terminal, finalization and publication faults. Capture remains failed if any fault, input changed during capture, incomplete denominator or output failure occurs; workflow exit zero is diagnostic delivery only.

## Five inert historical texts

`historical-text-origins.json` binds the five committed data members to the inspected run `37254827562`, artifact `11322239172`, ZIP SHA-256 `3e9ca590a613a7c1f2e4f70d50b42526f65a96773b9eae7cbb749fa697fc7957`, each exact ZIP member, and its original official runtime/analyzer archive version, hash and member bytes. The member list is exactly SELECTORS.json's five archive roles. A scoped historical/.gitattributes disables Git text normalization for these exact data assets; working files and committed blobs must both match their official member pins. These are reused historical inputs, not newly downloaded official archives and not current-runner files. They consume the five roles already counted above. They may be compared to new selected runner data; they cannot qualify the current hostfxr, runtime, tracing provider or analyzer selection.

## Executable wire schema and publication

SELECTORS.json remains the exact frozen conceptual contract. OUTPUT-SCHEMA.json is a distinct source-pinned wire protocol, schema version 2: finite record variants declare required/allowed keys and exact primitive types, and the packet executes those checks in addition to its source/hash/owner/budget/denominator checks. Its complete conceptualProjection maps every frozen required field to the actual wire position, or explicitly states that a fact is absent or outcomes are collapsed. For example, selector ID/kind/error live in the enclosing observation, errors can have a null file, ELF e_ident is checked but not detached, full PE region bounds are not a detached inventory, directory lstatBefore/After now denote descriptor fstat, and changed/new runner inventories live in evidence rather than duplicate summary arrays. The map does not fabricate unavailable facts or grant permission. The receipt explicitly sets frozenConceptualRequiredNamesEnforcedUnchanged=false and binds wireSchemaSha256. If the exact wire document cannot be captured, only an empty failed diagnostic fallback can be emitted; it cannot accept observations or a complete capture.

All JSON reports together, including summary and routing, reserve at most **32 MiB**. Raw public text plus all reports together reserve at most **64 MiB**. These are aggregate output ceilings, distinct from input caps. Bounded JSON tokens are sized incrementally with deadline checks before a file is opened; emission reserves each token before writing. Raw public text reserves its full bounded body before writing. Partial, failed and growing output attempts never refund reservations. No complete report is first materialized by a whole-document JSON encoder. Detached before-summary and before-routing reservation snapshots exclude their own report; the shared live counters enforce the full aggregate after those reports. Fixed entry diagnostics occur only before route invocation, when packet output has not begun. Publication failure remains NOT GREEN even if an earlier diagnostic exists.


The conservative content detector uses a bounded linear segment scan for credential/password/token/auth assignments and credential-bearing URLs, fixed literal private-key markers, and the retained inert config-reference checks before detaching text. It does not run ambiguous whole-input greedy regexes. XML is fed incrementally to an inert target that admits at most 64 depth and 65,536 nodes before retaining node rows; DTD/entities remain rejected. Attribute and retained text-fragment counts are conservatively bounded too. Status parsing admits lines/fields incrementally, retains fragments only for the nine reviewed fields, and joins each retained field once; no unknown value is emitted. Selected package-info and raw-text line lists admit each line before retaining it. A rejection records only safe codes and bounded byte hashes and makes capture incomplete. It is not a proof that every possible secret representation is detected. Credential/private-key paths are prohibited even if an eligible config or package file names them. Full package status, arbitrary package-owned files and unknown directory names are not detached; only reviewed fields, matching declarations, counts and bounded hashes are published. Package declarations do not establish authenticity or source correspondence.

The original inventory.py, its three source files and inner manifest are preserved byte-for-byte and are neither invoked nor imported. All original 44 ALC files, including the original 19 lifecycle files, are unchanged. Product base remains `v4.11.0 8333daa60e2f2ee456068369f94c141898cde875`. The only existing routing-manifest changes refresh their workflow pin after the narrowly added focus/job/exclusions. For all prior focus values, deleting the new job/option/exclusion clauses recovers the prior workflow bytes. Default/product/proof routes have no new implementation changes.

Before any publication or one data-only run, ROOT and an independent reviewer must review all new executable source, public-content detector, inert parsers, complete source/routing pins and this workflow inverse. SDK, collector, analyzer, target, proof and full namespace diagnostic routes remain disabled for this focus.
